desc:
Coupon codes and discounts for subscriptions, set up by Ecom Swift LLC. We create the codes in your billing provider, add a code field to checkout, and test the rules so launch offers and partner deals apply exactly as you intended.

## How do coupon codes work in a subscription?

A coupon is a rule stored in your billing provider that reduces what a customer pays. It can take a percentage or a fixed amount off, and it can apply once, for a set number of billing periods, or for as long as the subscription lasts. The customer enters a code at checkout, or follows a link that applies it for them, and the provider recalculates the total.

Subscriptions make discounts more delicate than one-off sales. A discount that repeats forever cuts your revenue every month, while a discount that applies once may confuse a customer who expected it to continue. Deciding the duration up front, and showing it clearly, avoids both problems.

## Why clear discount rules protect your revenue

Offers are one of the quickest ways to get a hesitant visitor to subscribe, but a badly built offer causes harm. Codes with no expiry date keep circulating on coupon sites. Codes with no use limit get shared far beyond the audience you meant. A code that works on the wrong plan sells your most expensive tier at a price you never planned.

A good setup keeps the offer attractive to the right people and closed to everyone else. Limits on date, plan, first-time customers and total redemptions turn a discount into a controlled campaign. The customer also benefits, because the invoice shows the discount line plainly and there is no argument about what was promised.

## What a well-built discount setup includes

- Coupons created in your billing provider with a clear internal name and a customer-facing code.
- Percentage-off and fixed-amount options, matched to your pricing.
- A duration for each coupon: once, repeating for a set number of months, or forever.
- An expiry date and a maximum number of redemptions.
- Restrictions by plan, so a code cannot be used on a tier it was not meant for.
- A first-time customer rule, so existing subscribers cannot reuse a new-customer offer.
- A code field on checkout, with clear messages for invalid or expired codes.
- Links that apply a code automatically, for emails, ads and partner pages.
- The discount shown as its own line on invoices and receipts.
- Unique codes for partners, with a report of how often each one was used.

## How we do the work

First we agree your offers on paper: what each one gives, who may use it and when it ends. Then we create the coupons in your provider account and add the code field to your checkout. We test every code, including the ones that should fail: an expired code, a code used past its limit, a code on the wrong plan, and a returning customer trying a first-time offer.

The Basic package covers a small set of codes with expiry and limits. The Standard package adds plan rules, first-time customer rules and auto-apply links, and checks that invoices display the discount. The Premium package adds partner codes, one level of referral rewards and a redemption report by code, with handover notes so you can create new codes yourself. We build the mechanics, and you decide the campaign. Ecom Swift LLC does not promise that an offer will lift sign-ups, since that depends on your audience and your price.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Give every code an end date and a redemption limit.
- Name codes clearly so the team can tell campaigns apart.
- Say on the page whether the discount applies once or every month.
- Use unique codes for partners so each channel can be measured.
- Test an expired code and a misused code before announcing the offer.

**Avoid:**
- Creating a forever discount without checking what it does to long-term revenue.
- Reusing one code across every campaign.
- Stacking several offers that were never meant to combine.
- Leaving old codes active after the campaign has ended.
- Letting customers discover the discount only after they have paid.

## Who this is for

This service suits a SaaS owner planning a launch offer or a holiday sale who needs the codes ready and tested. It suits a team that works with affiliates or partners and wants separate codes for each of them. It also suits a business that wants to bring back lapsed subscribers with a returning-customer discount.

## What we need and how to begin

Send us a short description of each offer you want, the plans it applies to and the dates it should run. Tell us which billing provider you use. We need developer or collaborator access to your app and a team role in your provider account, never a password. Once you order, we reply with a checklist, confirm the rules with you in writing, and share a test link before anything goes live.
